title: The votes for Congress's non-legislative powers
ask: Give the vote required for each: a canvass tie, a contested presidential inability, revoking martial law, amnesty, a treaty, war, amending the Constitution, impeaching, convicting.
items: Canvass tie for President or VP: a majority of all the Members of both Houses, voting separately (Art. VII, Sec. 4)
Contested inability of the President: two-thirds of both Houses, voting separately (Art. VII, Sec. 11)
Revoking or extending martial law or the suspension of the writ: a majority of all the Members, voting jointly (Art. VII, Sec. 18)
Amnesty: concurrence of a majority of all the Members of Congress (Art. VII, Sec. 19)
Treaty: two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate (Art. VII, Sec. 21)
War: two-thirds of both Houses in joint session, voting separately (Art. VI, Sec. 23(1))
Proposing amendments or a revision: three-fourths of all the Members (Art. XVII, Sec. 1)
Impeaching: one-third of all the Members of the House (Art. XI, Sec. 3(3)–(4))
Convicting: two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate (Art. XI, Sec. 3(6))
hook: Separately unless the text says jointly; only martial law pools the votes.

title: Why the canvass survived adjournment sine die (Pimentel, 2004)
ask: Why could the Joint Committee keep canvassing the 2004 presidential votes after Congress adjourned sine die?
items: Adjournment sine die ends the regular session, not the term of Congress (until noon of June 30; Art. VI, Secs. 4 and 7)
Art. VI, Sec. 15 concerns regular sessions and the 30-day recess, not the term
Canvassing as the National Board of Canvassers is non-legislative and continues until done
A board of canvassers is not functus officio until it completes its work; its membership may change
The joint session may reconvene without a call from the President
The Senate's own rules and the 1992 and 1998 precedents allow canvassing in recess
src: Pimentel v. Joint Committee of Congress (2004)

title: The special election when both offices are vacant (Art. VII, Sec. 10)
ask: State the rules on the special election for President and Vice-President.
items: Congress convenes at 10 AM of the third day after the vacancy, without need of a call
Within seven days it enacts a law calling a special election
The election is held not earlier than 45 days nor later than 60 days from the call
The bill is deemed certified and becomes law on approval on third reading
Appropriations come from current appropriations, exempt from Art. VI, Sec. 25(4)
The convening cannot be suspended nor the election postponed
No special election if the vacancy occurs within 18 months before the next presidential election
hook: 3rd day, 7 days, 45 to 60 days, no election within 18 months.

title: Congress and martial law after Padilla
ask: What must Congress do, and what need it not do, after the President proclaims martial law or suspends the writ?
items: Receive the President's report within 48 hours
Convene within 24 hours, without a call, if not in session
Revoke, if it wishes, by a majority of all its Members voting jointly; the President cannot set the revocation aside
Extend only on the President's initiative, in the same manner, if the rebellion persists and public safety requires
It need not meet in joint session merely to express support or concurrence; each House may use its own rules
If either House resolves to revoke, Congress must convene jointly to vote
src: Art. VII, Sec. 18; Padilla v. Congress (2017)
hook: Meet jointly only to vote jointly.

title: Amnesty versus pardon
items: Amnesty needs the concurrence of a majority of all the Members of Congress; pardon is the President's alone
Amnesty is a public act (judicial notice); pardon is private and must be pleaded and proved
Amnesty covers classes of persons, usually for political offenses; pardon covers individuals
Amnesty may come before or after prosecution; pardon only after conviction by final judgment
Amnesty looks backward and abolishes the offense; pardon looks forward and forgives the punishment
Pardon does not restore the right to hold office or vote unless it says so, and never the civil indemnity
src: Art. VII, Sec. 19; Gatmaytan, Government Structure, ch. 6
hook: Amnesty forgets the offense; pardon forgives the penalty.

title: The steps of treaty-making (Pimentel, 2005)
ask: List the steps in making a treaty, and who takes each.
items: Negotiation: the President, as sole organ, or agents with full powers
Signature: authenticates the text and shows good faith; does not bind
Ratification: the President, as head of state, accepts the treaty
Concurrence: two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate, in the ratification
Exchange of the instruments of ratification: entry into force
hook: Negotiate, sign, ratify, concur, exchange: the Senate concurs; it never ratifies.

title: When an executive agreement will do (Saguisag)
ask: When may the President use an executive agreement instead of a treaty?
items: Not for the initial entry of foreign military bases, troops or facilities: that needs a treaty (Art. XVIII, Sec. 25)
It must be traceable to express or implied authority: the Constitution, a treaty or a law
It must stay within the treaty or law it implements: no new or expanded obligations
It must be consistent with the Constitution and the laws; it is inferior to treaties and statutes
Otherwise the form follows the parties' intent; an exchange of notes will do (Bayan Muna)
src: Saguisag v. Ochoa (2016); Bayan Muna v. Romulo (2011)
hook: Entry needs a treaty; implementation needs only authority.

title: Withdrawing from a treaty (Pangilinan guidelines)
ask: When may the President withdraw from a treaty without the Senate?
items: Leeway to withdraw from a treaty bona fide deemed contrary to the Constitution or the laws; reviewable for grave abuse
Not unilaterally if the treaty was entered into pursuant to a prior law, or affirmed by a later law, unless that law is repealed
Not unilaterally if the Senate conditioned its concurrence on its concurrence in withdrawal
In a conflict between a statute and a treaty, the statute prevails
Laid down as guides for future cases: the Rome Statute petitions were dismissed as moot
hook: Two mirrors: a law behind it, or the Senate's condition.

title: Emergency powers under Art. VI, Sec. 23(2)
ask: State the conditions for the delegation of emergency powers to the President.
items: War or other national emergency
Delegation by law
For a limited period
Subject to the restrictions Congress prescribes
To carry out a declared national policy
The powers end at the next adjournment unless sooner withdrawn by resolution
src: Art. VI, Sec. 23(2); David v. Macapagal-Arroyo

title: Impeachable officers and the grounds
ask: Who may be impeached, and on what grounds?
items: The President, the Vice-President, the Members of the Supreme Court, the Members of the Constitutional Commissions, the Ombudsman
Grounds: culpable violation of the Constitution, treason, bribery, graft and corruption, other high crimes, betrayal of public trust
All other officers are removed as provided by law, not by impeachment
What counts as betrayal of public trust is a political question for Congress (Francisco)
src: Art. XI, Sec. 2; Francisco v. House

title: The House's impeachment periods (first mode)
ask: Give the steps and periods for a first-mode impeachment complaint in the House.
items: A verified complaint by a Member, or by a citizen with a Member's endorsement
Included in the Order of Business within 10 session days
Referred to the Committee within 3 session days thereafter
Committee report and resolution within 60 session days of referral, by a majority of all its Members
Calendared for the House within 10 session days of receipt
One-third of all the Members to affirm or override; each vote recorded

title: When an impeachment proceeding is initiated
ask: When is an impeachment proceeding deemed initiated, starting the one-year bar?
items: First mode: when the complaint is filed and referred to the Committee (Francisco; Gutierrez)
First mode: when a verified and endorsed complaint is not included in the Order of Business, or not referred, within the constitutional periods (Duterte, Resolution)
First mode: when a verified and endorsed or referred complaint is left unacted on at adjournment sine die (Duterte, Resolution)
Second mode: on valid endorsement by one-third of all the Members (Duterte, Resolution)
Two complaints referred at the same time are one proceeding (Gutierrez)
hook: Referred, lapsed, or left at sine die; or one-third signs.

title: Quo warranto versus impeachment (Sereno)
ask: Distinguish quo warranto from impeachment as ways of removing an impeachable officer.
items: Quo warranto tests title (eligibility at appointment or election); impeachment tests fitness (acts in office)
Quo warranto is judicial; impeachment is political
Quo warranto is brought by the State through the Solicitor General; impeachment starts in the House
Quo warranto ousts an officer who never validly held office (de facto); impeachment removes a de jure officer
Prescription does not run against the State in quo warranto
Both may proceed at the same time: different causes and reliefs
hook: Title or fitness? Before the oath, or after.

title: What an impeachment judgment does and does not do
ask: State the effects of a conviction in an impeachment case.
items: Removal from office
Disqualification to hold any office under the Republic
Nothing more: impeachment is political, not civil, criminal or administrative
The convicted officer remains liable to prosecution, trial and punishment according to law
No forfeiture of retirement benefits by the judgment alone: deemed involuntarily retired (Re: Corona)
No pardon in cases of impeachment (Art. VII, Sec. 19)
src: Art. XI, Sec. 3(7); Re: Letter of Mrs. Corona (2021)
hook: Takes the office, never the pension.

title: When the Court will (not) step into an impeachment
ask: Give the conditions under which the Supreme Court will rule on a challenge to an impeachment step.
items: A limit the Constitution itself sets is invoked (modes, periods, votes, the one-year bar, due process); not whether the acts are impeachable (Francisco)
The case is live: not after an accepted conviction (Corona), void Articles (Generillo), or transmittal to the Senate (Torreon)
The remedy is proper: certiorari or prohibition for grave abuse; not mandamus to set the Senate's timetable (Generillo)
The Court never decides when, who or whether to remove (Duterte)
src: Francisco; Corona v. Senate; Generillo; Torreon; Duterte v. House

title: What the 2026 Resolution changed in Duterte v. House
ask: How did the January 28, 2026 Resolution change the reasoning of the July 25, 2025 Decision?
items: Session day: a calendar day with a plenary session, not a legislative day
The fourth complaint is barred because the first complaint's periods lapsed, not because it used the second mode
No priority between the two modes, subject to the first-mode timelines
Due process: evidence available to all Members at plenary; the full hearing is at the Senate trial
Unchanged: the Articles are barred and void, and no proceeding before February 6, 2026
hook: Calendar days; the lapse, not the mode; no priority; hearing at the Senate.
